sara_support: Heads up — getting a customer escalation: hostedapi eu1 showing a big 502 spike right after TLS cert rotation at ~12:02 UTC. Customer traces show upstream closed stream, they see 502 on all text-generation endpoints.

chao_sre: Can you paste a sample trace id and the ingress logs? Also which LB rolled the cert (frontdoor vs edge-gw)?

sara_support: Trace IDs: trace=gf4k2q and trace=gf4k7p. From support logs looks like frontdoor pool rolled cert at 12:01:45 according to deploy-bot. Errors start ~12:03.

deploy-bot: rolled cert bundle fwd-cert-v2025-03 to frontdoor-eu1 at 2025-03-14T12:01:45Z by pipeline cert-rotator (sha: a1b2c3).

mike_ops: Seeing a lot of this in nginx error log on frontdoor nodes: `2025/03/14 12:03:02 [error] 1024#0: *789 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.23.45.67, server: hostedapi, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/2.0"`

mike_ops: Also TLS logs show handshake aborts with `alert handshake_failure` from some client IPs. Could be the new cert bundle missing a required intermediate or failing SNI mapping to backend pool.

chao_sre: If TLS handshake fails at LB, upstream shouldn't get requests — but we see 502s (upstream closed). That suggests frontdoor accepted but then failed to connect to edge-gw backend. Need to check SNI/ALPN changes: did cert rotation change CN or SANs?

anika_eng: The cert rotation only replaced chain; SANs unchanged. But the new bundle has stricter TLS1.3 ciphers set by the CA (ECDHE_AESGCM) and our edge-gw fleet still has some older envoy instances with ALPN mismatch. We have a partial rollout — some frontdoor nodes updated, some upstreams not.

sara_support: Customer impact list: 3 major customers reported 502s across multiple regions but concentrated in eu1. They included curl samples: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.eu1.redwood.ai/v1/generate` returns HTTP/2 502.

chao_sre: Short repro I ran: `openssl s_client -connect frontdoor-eu1.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.eu1.redwood.ai -alpn h2` shows handshake completes on some nodes, but others fail with `no protocols available`.

mike_ops: Quick mitigation options: 1) roll back cert bundle on frontdoor to previous version (fast but needs manual rollback and reissuance window). 2) Hotfix envoy on older edge-gw instances to accept new ALPN/ciphers (deploy small). 3) Temporarily route eu1 traffic to eu2 fallback by adjusting routing policy.

anika_eng: Recommend immediate step: take frontdoor nodes that have the new cert out of LB (drain) to stop sending to mixed upstreams, then rollout a small envoy patch to edge-gw to accept the new cipher suite. If we can't patch quickly, rollback cert.

sara_support: Customer asked for ETA — can we give an initial mitigation?

chao_sre: I'm going to start draining updated frontdoor nodes now (12:07). If that reduces 502s in 5-10m we know rollout mismatch is root.

mike_ops: I started a canary envoy restart on 3 edge-gw hosts, pushing an env var to enable fallback ALPN. If that succeeds, we can accelerate patch.

anika_eng: Creating an incident page and will add commands and sample logs. Noting followups: check cert chain includes required intermediate for some older clients, validate OCSP stapling behavior on certs.

sara_support: Thanks team — I'll update the customer: "We've identified a cert rotation + ALPN mismatch between frontdoor and some older edge gateways causing upstream closes and 502s. We're draining affected frontdoor nodes and patching edge gateways; ETA 30-60m for initial mitigation." :thumbsup:

chao_sre: Update 12:25 — after draining rolled frontdoor nodes, 502 rate dropped ~80% in eu1. Still seeing a few nodes lagging, continuing patch.

mike_ops: Patch succeeded on canaries, prepping scale. Will post host list and restart plan in incident doc.

sara_support: Customer notified and will keep them updated. Closing this thread for the immediate escalation, continuing ops in incident doc.
